items.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance derived myocardial strain: applications, acquisition techniques, analysis, and reporting. A Scientific Statement of the Society for Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance, Radiological Society of North America, and the European Association of Cardiovascular Imaging of the ESC.
items.abstract: Myocardial strain imaging enables quantification of cardiac deformation. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging (CMR) is well suited for strain assessment due to the ability to image in any given plane with high spatial and contrast resolution. CMR strain measures have incremental diagnostic and prognostic utility over conventional clinical imaging parameters across disease states. Routine integration of CMR strain assessment in clinical practice has been hindered by the lack of agreement on imaging protocols and analysis methods, variability due to noise sensitivity, and a paucity of robust normative age-, sex- and ethnicity-specific reference ranges. In recognition of the expanding applications of strain techniques in clinical and research CMR, this joint SCMR/RSNA/EACVI scientific statement integrates data from original research studies, guidelines, and opinions from experts across the field to guide responsible and evidence-based utilization of CMR strain.

items.title: Real-World Predictors and Temporal Trends in Intravascular Imaging Use During Percutaneous Coronary Intervention in a Publicly Funded Health System.
items.abstract: Intravascular imaging (IVI) improves clinical outcomes in percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), yet real-world utilisation remains inconsistent. We evaluated temporal trends and determinants of IVI use within a large publicly funded, non-fee-for-service, healthcare system. All PCI procedures performed across Queensland public hospitals between 2016 and 2023 were analysed using registry data. The primary outcome was IVI use. Independent predictors were assessed using multivariable analysis. Among 39,136 PCI procedures, IVI was used in 9.0% overall and increased from 5.6% in 2016 to 16.5% in 2023 (p trend =0.002). Procedural complexity was the primary determinant: left main PCI (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 7.84; 95% confidence interval [CI] 5.26-11.69), intravascular lithotripsy (aOR 8.51; 95% CI 3.78-19.15), and bifurcation lesions (aOR 1.34; 95% CI 1.01-1.78) were independent predictors. Conversely, ST-elevation myocardial infarction predicted lower use (aOR 0.49; 95% CI 0.42-0.59). Higher operator procedural volume was associated with increased IVI use (aOR 1.25; 95% CI 1.00-1.54). While operator training era and institutional factors were significant in unadjusted models, associations were attenuated after accounting for hospital-level clustering, suggesting strong influence of local hospital processes and culture toward IVI. IVI use has increased but remains underutilised. Adoption is driven primarily by procedural complexity and operator-level factors, with persistent inter-hospital variability. These findings highlight an ongoing evidence-practice gap and support system-level strategies to standardise IVI use in contemporary PCI.

items.title: The Added Value of Vessel Wall MRI Over CTA for Differentiating Large-Artery Atherosclerotic and Cardioembolic Stroke in the Anterior and Posterior Circulations.
items.abstract: Differentiation between stroke etiologies is essential for secondary prevention; however, etiologic classification remains challenging in many ischemic strokes. We evaluated whether magnetic resonance vessel wall imaging (VWI) plaque markers improve computed tomography angiography (CTA)-based differentiation between cardioembolic (CE) and large-artery atherosclerotic (LAA) stroke in the anterior and posterior circulations, as a step toward improving etiologic classification beyond current criteria. We retrospectively included patients with unilateral anterior or posterior circulation ischemic stroke between June 2022 and April 2024 across an academic health system, classified as LAA or CE according to modified TOAST criteria. Imaging markers included CTA-derived noncalcified plaque extent (>30% stenosis), VWI-derived intracranial plaque enhancement (IPE) extent, and intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) presence, restricted to arterial segments upstream from the infarct. Given potential territory-specific plaque differences, analyses were stratified by circulation. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of CTA and VWI markers with stroke etiology. Associations with LAA were summarized using adjusted odds ratios (aOR; plaque extent variables per 1-SD increase). Overall performance for discriminating between LAA and CE etiologies was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Among 193 patients (median age, 70 years; 60% male), 137 had anterior circulation strokes (65 LAA, 72 CE) and 56 had posterior circulation strokes (38 LAA, 18 CE). In anterior circulation strokes, VWI markers improved discrimination over CTA alone (AUC, 0.57 for CTA alone vs 0.76 for CTA+VWI; p<0.001); CTA-derived noncalcified plaque extent (aOR, 1.7; p=0.02), IPH (aOR, 7.0; p<0.001), and IPE extent (aOR, 1.9; p=0.005) were independently associated with LAA. In posterior circulation strokes, IPE extent improved discrimination over CTA alone (AUC, 0.77 for CTA alone vs 0.84 for CTA+VWI; p=0.02); IPE extent (aOR, 2.2; p=0.02) and CTA-derived noncalcified plaque extent (aOR, 5.9; p=0.002) were independently associated with LAA. IPH was not significantly associated with posterior circulation stroke etiology (p=0.26). VWI adds complementary value for differentiating LAA and CE stroke etiologies in both vascular territories, supporting a pragmatic CTA-VWI approach for etiologic characterization beyond stenosis assessment alone.

items.title: [Inclusive Medicine in Germany: Recommendations for Action and Future Prospects from the "Inclusive Medicine 2026" Symposium in Fulda].
items.abstract: People with intellectual disabilities (ID) experience a high burden of disease, substantially reduced life expectancy, and limited access to healthcare services. Despite international human rights commitments, significant inequalities in prevention, health promotion, and healthcare persist compared with the general population. The aim of the Inclusive Medicine Conference 2026 was to identify key challenges and to develop participatory recommendations for a sustainable and inclusive healthcare system. A multidisciplinary and participatory future workshop was conducted during the Inclusive Medicine Conference in Fulda, involving approximately 100 participants from healthcare, academia, disability support services, self-advocacy organizations, health insurers, as well as people with ID and their relatives. Discussions took place in four moderated working groups focusing on financing, responsibility, coordination, and education. Recommendations were documented, discussed in plenary, and consolidated. The main challenges did not lie in the lack of medical possibilities but in structural deficiencies of the healthcare system. Key deficits were identified in financing, allocation of responsibilities, cross-sectoral coordination, and education and training. Ten recommendations for action were developed from the discussions. In addition, a nationwide Research and Translation Network for Inclusive Health was established to systematically integrate healthcare delivery, research, evidence generation, and knowledge translation. The challenges of inclusive healthcare are well described. However, the primary need today lies less in further problem identification than in the development, evaluation, and sustainable implementation of evidence-based models of care. Interdisciplinary networks, living labs, and shared data infrastructures represent key prerequisites for achieving this goal. Menschen mit intellektueller Beeinträchtigung (IB) weisen eine hohe Krankheitslast, eine deutlich reduzierte Lebenserwartung und einen erschwerten Zugang zur Gesundheitsversorgung auf. Trotz internationaler menschenrechtlicher Verpflichtungen bestehen gegenüber der Allgemeinbevölkerung weiterhin erhebliche Ungleichheiten in Prävention, Gesundheitsförderung und medizinischer Versorgung. Ziel des Fachtags Inklusive Medizin 2026 war die Identifikation zentraler Herausforderungen sowie die Entwicklung partizipativ erarbeiteter Handlungsempfehlungen für eine zukunftsfähige inklusive Gesundheitsversorgung.Es wurde eine multiprofessionelle und partizipative Zukunftswerkstatt mit rund 100 Teilnehmenden aus Gesundheitsversorgung, Wissenschaft, Eingliederungshilfe, Selbstvertretung, Kostenträgern sowie Menschen mit IB und Angehörigen während des Fachtags Inklusive Medizin in Fulda durchgeführt. Die Bearbeitung erfolgte in vier moderierten Arbeitsgruppen zu den Themen Finanzierung, Verantwortung, Koordination und Ausbildung. Handlungsempfehlungen wurden dokumentiert, im Plenum diskutiert und zusammengeführt.Die zentralen Herausforderungen lagen nicht in fehlenden medizinischen Möglichkeiten, sondern in strukturellen Defiziten des Versorgungssystems. Identifiziert wurden insbesondere Defizite in Finanzierung, Verantwortungszuweisung, sektorenübergreifender Koordination sowie Aus- und Weiterbildung. Aus den Diskussionen wurden zehn Handlungsempfehlungen abgeleitet. Im Rahmen des Fachtags wurde ein bundesweiter Forschungs- und Transferverbund gegründet, der Versorgung, Forschung, Evidenzgenerierung und Transfer systematisch vernetzen soll.Die Herausforderungen einer inklusiven Gesundheitsversorgung sind gut beschrieben. Der zentrale Handlungsbedarf liegt heute jedoch weniger in der Problemanalyse als vielmehr in der Entwicklung, Evaluation und nachhaltigen Implementierung evidenzbasierter Versorgungsmodelle. Interdisziplinäre Netzwerke, Gesundheitsreallabore und gemeinsame Datenstrukturen bilden hierfür zentrale Voraussetzungen.

items.title: Making space for cures: Conditioning for autologous hematopoietic stem cell gene therapies.
items.abstract: Although allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation has long been the only curative therapy for nonmalignant blood diseases, recent clinical successes have demonstrated the transformative potential of autologous gene therapies as definitive treatments for these disorders. By providing durable life-changing clinical benefit while reducing the need for suitable allogeneic donors and avoiding immunologic complications like graft rejection and graft-versus-host disease, autologous transplantation with genetically modified hematopoietic stem cells provides a potentially safer and, in some respects, more accessible pathway to cure. However, several formidable barriers still prevent broader use of autologous gene therapy, including the risk of adverse acute and chronic effects from the busulfan-based conditioning regimens used to deplete host hematopoietic stem cells before transplant. In this article, we define the role transplant conditioning regimens play in autologous gene therapy, including contrasting the goals of care in this setting with those for stem cell transplantation for malignancies. We also discuss the conditioning strategies that are used by approved and select investigational autologous gene therapies to date, while highlighting exciting preclinical and clinical advances aimed at making transplant conditioning safer for myriad nonmalignant and malignant disease applications.

items.title: Practical MRI interpretation of intracranial metastases before and after multidisciplinary management: a pictorial review.
items.abstract: Intracranial metastases represent the most common form of brain tumors in adults. Their diagnosis and post-treatment evaluation are routine tasks in neuroradiology. In this setting, radiologists collaborate with neuro-oncologists, neurosurgeons, radiation oncologists, and other specialists to guide multidisciplinary treatment strategies and assess their response. A well-appointed radiologist should therefore be familiar with current treatment paradigms and their respective manifestations on imaging. This pictorial review begins by reviewing imaging findings of intracranial metastases, emphasizing features germane to management decision-making. Major treatment modalities including radiation, systemic, and surgical approaches, are discussed. The focus of this article is then post-treatment imaging appearance of intracranial metastases, and the major complications associated with each treatment modality are surveyed. Additionally, applications of advanced imaging techniques to differentiate residual or recurrent metastatic disease from treatment-related changes are explored.

Combined pharmacological targeting of NAD + metabolism preserves central and peripheral axons in an ex vivo model of Wallerian degeneration.
items.abstract: Wallerian degeneration (WD) is a conserved axonal self-destruction program implicated in a spectrum of neurological conditions, including peripheral neuropathies, traumatic brain injury, and possibly neurodegenerative diseases. Wallerian degeneration is triggered by depletion of the NAD + -synthesizing enzyme NMNAT2, subsequent NMN accumulation, and activation of the NAD + -hydrolyzing SARM1, ultimately driving axonal fragmentation. While pharmacological inhibition of SARM1 is an emerging therapeutic strategy, current challenges due to paradoxical toxicity with orthosteric base-exchange SARM1 inhibitors highlight the need for alternative approaches. We have shown before that targeted modulation of NAD + metabolism centered on NAMPT inhibition (FK866) and nicotinic acid riboside (NaR) supplementation, and enhanced by DLK-JNK inhibition (GNE-3511) can prevent or suppress SARM1 activation and robustly protect axotomized axons in vitro. In this paper, we investigated the efficacy of combined treatments that modulate SARM1 triggers and block DLK-JNK WD in an explant model of WD using sciatic and optic nerve segments. Our findings show that our combination treatment robustly preserved the integrity of axons in the nerve up to 7 days in culture, reduced ongoing degeneration of axoskeleton, and suppressed SARM1 NADase and DLK-JNK activation by metabolomic and immunoblot analyses. Effects were similar to those of the orthosteric inhibitor NB-3 and perhaps better for stabilizing neurofilaments. Delayed initiation of the combination regimen but not NB-3 were robustly protective, indicating the presence of a therapeutic window of at least 24 h. Our results demonstrate that targeted modulation of NAD + metabolic pathways and inhibition of DLK-JNK signaling confers significant axon protection, further supporting the role of these approaches as viable therapeutic alternatives to direct orthosteric SARM1 inhibitors.

items.title: Phenotype and prognosis of primary sclerosing cholangitis-autoimmune hepatitis variant syndrome.
items.abstract: A subset of patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) exhibits features of autoimmune hepatitis (AIH), referred to as PSC-AIH variant syndrome (VS). Data on the phenotype and prognosis of VS remain limited. We compared clinical characteristics and outcomes of patients with VS and PSC without VS (non-VS). This retrospective cohort study included patients with PSC followed at a tertiary referral center. VS was defined as moderate-to-severe interface hepatitis on liver histology combined with at least one of the following: alanine aminotransferase ≥5 × upper limit of normal (ULN), IgG ≥1.5 × ULN, or smooth muscle antibody titer ≥1:80. Twenty-eight patients with VS and 274 non-VS patients were included. At diagnosis, VS patients were younger (median 20 vs. 30 years, p < 0.001), less frequently had inflammatory bowel disease (46.4% vs. 77.7%, p = 0.001), and more often presented with cirrhosis (25% vs. 8%, p = 0.010). Median follow-up was 9.9 years. Adjusted transplant-free survival was similar between groups (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.11-1.00; p = 0.051). After adjustment, VS was associated with a lower risk of liver-related events (HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.09-0.80; p = 0.019). Despite more frequent cirrhosis at diagnosis, patients with VS had comparable transplant-free survival and lower adjusted hazard of liver-related events.

Impact of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease on the development of hepatocellular carcinoma after HCV cure.
items.abstract: The impact of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) development after hepatitis C virus (HCV) elimination remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to clarify this association in a cohort of patients stratified by fibrosis severity. We analyzed the data of 2,596 eligible patients obtained from a multicenter database between 2014 and 2025. The FIB-4 index was used to assess fibrosis status, with patients categorized into three groups: 3.25. Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models were used to evaluate factors independently associated with HCC development. The median follow-up duration was 6.7 years. MASLD was present in 975 patients (36.3%) and was more frequent among men and patients with diabetes. During follow-up, 156 patients (6.0%) developed de novo HCC. Patients with MASLD had a higher cumulative incidence of HCC than those without MASLD (log-rank test, P 3.25. Older age, male sex, lower albumin level, and higher AFP level at post-treatment week 12 were also independently associated with HCC development, whereas individual cardiometabolic risk factors were not significant after adjustment. MASLD was significantly associated with an increased risk of HCC after HCV cure, even among patients with intermediate FIB-4 values of 1.45-3.25. These findings support the need for tailored surveillance and management strategies.

items.title: Impact of histologic hepatic steatosis on virological response to nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy in patients with chronic hepatitis B.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B remains a major cause of cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma worldwide. We investigated whether histologic hepatic steatosis affects hepatitis B virus deoxyribonucleic acid (HBV DNA) suppression in patients receiving antiviral therapy. This retrospective observational study included 307 adult patients with chronic hepatitis B who received tenofovir or entecavir therapy and underwent pretreatment liver biopsy. Demographic, laboratory, virological, radiological, and histopathological data were retrieved from the electronic medical record system. Laboratory parameters included complete blood count, liver function tests, alpha-fetoprotein, renal function tests, and lipid profile. Histopathological evaluation included fibrosis stage, histologic activity index, and hepatic steatosis percentage. Ultrasonographic findings included hepatic steatosis, liver echotexture, and contour. The primary outcome was HBV DNA suppression at 12 months. Long-term virological response was evaluated as time to first HBV DNA suppression during follow-up (maximum 60 months). A total of 307 patients receiving entecavir or tenofovir were included, of whom 258 (84.0%) achieved HBV DNA suppression at 12 months. Patients without suppression had higher baseline aspartate aminotransferase, histologic activity index, histologic steatosis, and baseline log10 HBV DNA levels (all P < .05). Histologic steatosis ≥5% was more frequent in patients without suppression (42.9% vs 23.6%, P = .005). In multivariable analysis, steatosis ≥5% (odds ratio 0.365, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.179-0.746; P = .006) and higher baseline log10 HBV DNA (odds ratio 0.842, 95% CI 0.751-0.944; P = .003) were associated with a lower likelihood of 12-month suppression, with similar findings in the parsimonious sensitivity model. Kaplan-Meier analysis showed delayed suppression with steatosis (log-rank P = .016); however, this association was not significant in the conventional adjusted Cox model (hazard ratio 0.900, 95% CI 0.689-1.175; P = .438), and a significant time-dependent interaction indicated non-proportionality (P < .001). Histologic steatosis and higher baseline log10 HBV DNA were associated with a lower likelihood of 12-month HBV DNA suppression. However, an independent longitudinal association with time to suppression was not demonstrated. Residual confounding by unmeasured metabolic factors cannot be excluded.

items.title: The landscape of hepatocellular carcinoma recurrence after liver transplantation: a nationwide 14-year study.
items.abstract: Recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (r-HCC) remains a major determinant of post-transplant (LT) outcomes. The 2024 ILTS-ILCA consensus highlighted the need for contemporary data assessing how evolving selection criteria and therapeutic strategies over the past 15 years have influenced prognosis. We conducted a retrospective study including all patients diagnosed with r-HCC following LT between 2008 and 2020 across 15 French transplant centres. Recurrence patterns, post-recurrence survival, and overall transplant outcomes were analysed, including temporal trends and the impact of AFP model implementation in 2013. We analysed 388 patients with r-HCC, median time to recurrence was 19.1 months, with 26.3% occurring beyond 3 years. Earlier recurrence was associated with tumour-related factors (AFP and Milan criteria, αFP kinetics), and later recurrence with patient-related factors (HCV recurrence, alcohol relapse, grade 2 obesity). Following AFP model implementation, time to recurrence shortened (p<0.001). Surgical/ablative treatments improved survival in r-HCC in a subgroup of patients with single organ involvement of liver, lung or lymph nodes. Survival did not improve between patients diagnosed before 2016, between 2016 and 2018, or after 2018 (p=0.09). Calcineurin inhibitors or mycophenolate mofetil had no impact on survival, whereas mTOR inhibitor use was associated with significantly longer survival (20.7 vs 13.2 months, p=0.001). r-HCC is a heterogeneous disease distinct from HCC in non-transplanted patients. Earlier recurrences following extended selection criteria implementation warrant caution. Surgical/ablative approaches should be prioritized even for extrahepatic disease. Despite expanded TKI options since 2016, outcomes of systemic treatment did not show statistical improvement. Post-recurrence mTOR inhibitors should be evaluated in clinical trials. This nationwide cohort study provides updated data on recurrence of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) after liver transplantation in the modern era, a special population excluded from major HCC trials, highlighting major heterogeneity in patients' trajectories before and after recurrence, variations across eras of selection criteria and systemic therapies, and an urgent unmet need as the approval of second-generation TKIs after 2016 did not incrementally improve survival. The study results are important for transplant hepatologists and liver oncologists to optimize patient selection for liver transplantation, to individualize prolongation of surveillance beyond the current ILTS-ILCA 3-year window recommendation based on patient-related risk factors for late recurrences, and prioritize radical treatments with curative intent for selected patients with single organ involvement of liver, lungs or lymph nodes, rather than a blanket systemic-only approach. The retrospective design of the analysis does not allow for formal demonstration of superiority of therapeutic strategies, but provide evidence to design clinical trials on newer systemic agents such as immune-checkpoint inhibitors.

items.title: Effective treatment of orthotopic liver cancer with bifunctional embolization microspheres.
items.abstract: Transcatheter arterial chemoembolization (TACE) is a minimally invasive procedure used widely for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). However, embolization-induced hypoxia upregulates VEGF, and the resulting angiogenic response contributes to tumor recurrence, further limiting the efficacy of TACE against HCC. Herein, we present a multifunctional embolic microsphere system in which sorafenib (SRF) and calcium carbonate (CaCO 3 ) nanoparticles are rationally encapsulated within sodium hyaluronate microspheres (SRF-CaCO 3 @SH MSs) via microfluidic technology. The microspheres exhibited a bowl-shaped morphology with tunable diameters, which enhances in vivo embolic stability through mechanical interlocking between adjacent microspheres. In an acidic tumor microenvironment (TME), pH-triggered release of Ca²⁺ (23.9%) and SRF (65.7%) far exceeded neutral conditions. SRF-CaCO 3 @SH MSs maintained >85% HUVEC viability and reduced VX2 cell viability to 24.3%, showing maximal cytotoxicity under acidic conditions. After intra-arterial injection, the microspheres occluded tumor-feeding arteries; Ca²⁺ released in the acidic TME inhibited angiogenesis, and CaCO 3 neutralized TME acidity, counteracting immunosuppression. In a rabbit VX2 orthotopic HCC model, DSA-guided TACE achieved effective occlusion, slowest tumor growth, largest necrosis, and marked downregulation of CD31, Ki67, and VEGF, without systemic toxicity. Combining morphological design, pH-responsive occlusion, TME neutralization, and anti-angiogenesis, this embolic system synergistically enhances TACE and shows strong clinical potential. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Conventional liver cancer embolization frequently fails due to hypoxia-driven angiogenesis and subsequent tumor recurrence. We developed a dual-functional embolic microsphere (SRF-CaCO 3 @SH MS) that integrates stable vascular occlusion with active modulation of the tumor microenvironment. Utilizing microfluidics, we fabricated bowl-shaped sodium hyaluronate microspheres that mechanically interlock to ensure durable embolization. Under acidic tumor conditions, calcium carbonate neutralizes pH and releases Ca²⁺, which synergizes with sorafenib to inhibit angiogenesis and induce apoptosis. In a rabbit orthotopic HCC model, this system demonstrated superior tumor control and necrosis without inducing systemic toxicity. This work presents a microenvironment-responsive embolization strategy integrating durable vascular occlusion, pH modulation, and anti-angiogenic therapy.

items.title: Hepatocyte Serine Palmitoyltransferase 3 is essential for mitochondrial ceramide homeostasis and electron transport chain function.
items.abstract: Sphingolipids constitute essential membrane lipids that also function as signaling molecules mediating fundamental cellular processes. Disruption of constitutive sphingolipid metabolism contributes to a range of metabolic diseases. Sphingolipid biosynthesis is initiated by serine palmitoyltransferase (SPT), a heteromeric enzyme composed of Sptlc1 and either Sptlc2 or the less-characterized subunit Sptlc3. While the canonical Sptlc1/Sptlc2 complex generates most sphingolipids, Sptlc1/Sptlc3 produces non-canonical sphingolipids that remain poorly understood. Sptlc3 expression increases in liver disease in both mouse models and humans, yet its biological role remains unclear. To address this, we generated a liver-specific SPTLC3 knockout (SPT3-hKO) mouse model. Loss of SPTLC3 resulted in severe mitochondrial dysfunction in hepatocytes, characterized by reduced oxygen consumption, decreased ATP production, and elevated NADH/NAD + ratios with a concomitant increase in glycolytic activity. Mechanistically, we found a defect in the electron transport chain (ETC) which stemmed not from intrinsic impairment of the ETC complexes but rather from hindered electron flow between complex I and complex III likely due to reduced availability of Coenzyme Q. While atypical ceramides constituted (∼4% of total ceramides) when measured in liver homogenates, there measurements in mitochondria-enriched fractions revealed enrichment in this cell compartment. Together, our findings identify SPTLC3 as a critical modulator of mitochondrial ceramide composition and ETC function, revealing a specialized role for non-canonical sphingolipids in hepatocyte energy metabolism.

items.title: Beyond target presence: A cross-cancer contextual framework for siRNA therapeutics in solid tumors.
items.abstract: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) has achieved clinical success in liver-directed therapies, but its translation to solid tumors remains limited by heterogeneous delivery and context-dependent target dependence. This review compares non-small cell lung cancer, pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, breast cancer, glioblastoma, and hepatocellular carcinoma across four interconnected dimensions: resistance networks, tumor microenvironmental reprogramming, metastatic progression, and delivery-system design. We examine how bypass signaling and phenotypic plasticity influence target selection, how stromal and immune compartments shape therapeutic responses, and how disease stage and organ-specific barriers alter delivery requirements. We then assess representative clinical RNA interference programs to distinguish evidence of tissue exposure and target engagement from antitumor activity and established clinical benefit. Across these settings, tumor accumulation does not establish productive cytosolic delivery, and target knockdown alone does not ensure durable disease control. We propose a context-dependent framework that aligns functional target dependence with the intended cell population, tissue environment, treatment timing, and delivery route. Priorities include resistance-informed combinations, prospective validation of delivery biomarkers, repeat-dose safety assessment, and carrier designs whose functional benefits justify their manufacturing complexity. By linking mechanistic comparison with clinical evidence, this review identifies testable criteria for selecting patients, evaluating functional delivery, and advancing siRNA therapeutics for solid tumors.
